name: Bunny hop a bike
blurb: Lifting both wheels over an obstacle without clipping it. Genuinely useful for potholes and kerbs, and the foundation of most mountain-bike technique.
gear: A stick or a small obstacle
Flat ground and pads if you are nervous
steps: Learn the front wheel lift first: crouch, then explode up and back, pulling the bars towards your hips.
Learn the rear wheel lift separately: shift forward, drop your heels and scoop the pedals up behind you.
Combine them in sequence — front up, then push forward and scoop the rear — rather than trying to jump both at once.
Practise over a stick or a chalk line before anything solid.
Keep your arms and legs working as suspension, absorbing the landing.
Build the height gradually, always over something you can safely hit.
tips: Pulling straight up on the bars does nothing. The lift comes from a body movement back and up.
Practise over something soft. Clipping a kerb at speed sends you over the bars.
proof: You clear a 15 cm obstacle cleanly with both wheels, ten times in a row.
